methods.label: Count face interiors and the inner cube
methods.explanation:
A small cube has exactly one painted face precisely when it lies on an outer face but away from the original cube's edges. On each outer face, removing the boundary row along every edge leaves an \((n-2)\)-by-\((n-2)\) array. Thus the number with exactly one painted face is
\[
6(n-2)^2.
\]
These six groups do not overlap, because each counted cube touches exactly one outer face.

The completely unpainted cubes lie inside all the outer layers. They form a cube with \(n-2\) small cubes along each edge, giving
\[
(n-2)^3
\]
unpainted cubes. These descriptions include every cube in each requested category.

Equating the counts,
\[
6(n-2)^2=(n-2)^3.
\]
Since \(n>2\), the factor \((n-2)^2\) is positive and may be canceled. Hence \(6=n-2\), so \(\boxed{n=8}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
